title: KiranaBench: Can a Language Model Run a Neighbourhood Shop?
abstract: arXiv:2610.22980v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly evaluated on long-horizon tasks, including autonomously running a business. Existing benchmarks for this setting are almost exclusively English-language, Western in retail context, and single-agent, with the agent observing the business directly. We study how these results transfer to a multi-agent Indic setting. We introduce KiranaBench, a simulated Indian general store in which four roles (manager, cashier, helper, and bookkeeper) are each played by a separate LLM agent. Interactions with customers and suppliers occur in English, Hindi, or Hinglish, and product demand is calibrated to India's national Household Consumption Expenditure Survey. Evaluating four open-weight LLMs, we find that all fall far short of a fixed-rule shopkeeper baseline: the best model earns only one-eighth of the baseline's profit, and two models finish below an unmanaged shop. translated_title: KiranaBench：语言模型能经营一家社区小店吗？
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体正越来越多地在长时程任务上接受评估，其中包括自主经营一门生意。针对这一场景的现有基准几乎全部是英语的、以西方零售环境为背景的，并且是单智能体形式，由智能体直接观察业务运作。我们研究了这些结果如何迁移到多智能体的印度语境中。我们提出了KiranaBench——一个模拟的印度杂货店，其中四个角色（经理、收银员、帮手和记账员）分别由独立的LLM智能体扮演。与顾客和供应商的交互以英语、印地语或印地英语进行，产品需求则根据印度的全国家庭消费支出调查进行校准。在评估四个开源权重LLM后，我们发现所有模型都远逊于一个基于固定规则的店主基线：表现最好的模型仅获得基线利润的八分之一，还有两个模型的收益甚至低于一家无人管理的店铺。此外，性能表现也持续……
tldr: 论文提出多智能体印度杂货店模拟基准KiranaBench，评估发现四个开源LLM的经营利润均远低于固定规则店主基线，最佳模型仅获得其八分之一的利润。
en_tdlr: We introduce KiranaBench, a multi-agent simulated Indian general store benchmark, and find that all four open-weight LLMs earn far less profit than a fixed-rule shopkeeper baseline, with the best model earning only one-eighth of it.
